arxiv-2103-15097.title: Compound matrices in systems and control theory
arxiv-2103-15097.creator: Eyal Bar-Shalom, Michael Margaliot
arxiv-2103-15097.description: Abstract The multiplicative and additive compounds of a matrix play an important role in several fields of mathematics including geometry, multi-linear algebra, combinatorics, and the analysis of nonlinear time-varying dynamical systems. There is a growing interest in applications of these compounds, and their generalizations, in systems and control theory.

arxiv-2111-01822.title: Informative Planning in the Presence of Outliers
arxiv-2111-01822.creator: Weizhe Chen, Lantao Liu
arxiv-2111-01822.description: Abstract Informative planning seeks a sequence of actions that guide the robot to collect the most informative data to build a large-scale environmental model or learn a dynamical system. Existing work in informative planning mainly focuses on proposing new planners and applying them to various robotic applications such as environmental monitoring, autonomous exploration, and system identification.

arxiv-2203-03578.title: Unsupervised Quantum Circuit Learning in High Energy Physics
arxiv-2203-03578.creator: Andrea Delgado, Kathleen E. Hamilton
arxiv-2203-03578.description: Abstract Unsupervised training of generative models is a machine learning task that has many applications in scientific computing. In this work we evaluate the efficacy of using quantum circuit-based generative models to generate synthetic data of high energy physics processes. We use non-adversarial, gradient-based training of quantum circuit Born machines to generate joint distributions over 2 and 3 variables.

arxiv-2405-02414.title: Transforming graph states via Bell state measurements
arxiv-2405-02414.creator: Matthias C. Löbl, Love A. Pettersson, Stefano Paesani, Anders S. Sørensen
arxiv-2405-02414.description: Abstract Graph states are key resources for measurement-based quantum computing, which is particularly promising for photonic systems. Fusions are probabilistic Bell state measurements, measuring pairs of parity operators of two qubits. Fusions can be used to connect/entangle different graph states, making them a powerful resource for measurement-based and related fusion-based quantum computing.

arxiv-2407-01945.title: Indoor 3D Reconstruction with an Unknown Camera-Projector Pair
arxiv-2407-01945.creator: Zhaoshuai Qi, Yifeng Hao, Rui Hu, Wenyou Chang, Jiaqi Yang, Yanning Zhang
arxiv-2407-01945.description: Abstract Structured light-based method with a camera-projector pair (CPP) plays a vital role in indoor 3D reconstruction, especially for scenes with weak textures. Previous methods usually assume known intrinsics, which are pre-calibrated from known objects, or self-calibrated from multi-view observations. It is still challenging to reliably recover CPP intrinsics from only two views without any known objects.

arxiv-2412-05536.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Multimodal AI Models in Medical Imaging Diagnosis: From Data Augmentation to Preference-Based Comparison
arxiv-2412-05536.creator: Cailian Ruan *, Chengyue Huang, Yahe Yang
arxiv-2412-05536.description: Abstract This study introduces an evaluation framework for multimodal models in medical imaging diagnostics. We developed a pipeline incorporating data preprocessing, model inference, and preference-based evaluation, expanding an initial set of 500 clinical cases to 3,000 through controlled augmentation. Our method combined medical images with clinical observations to generate assessments, using Claude 3.5 Sonnet for independent evaluation against physician-authored diagnoses.

arxiv-2502-00902.title: Position: More Rigorous Software Engineering Would Improve Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research
arxiv-2502-00902.creator: Moritz Wolter, Lokesh Veeramacheneni
arxiv-2502-00902.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Moritz Wolter, Lokesh Veeramacheneni. Experimental verification and falsification of scholarly work are part of the scientific method’s core. To improve the Machine Learning-communities’ ability to verify results from prior work, we argue for more robust software engineering.

arxiv-2502-08300.title: Unbounded dynamics for three dimensional vector fields
arxiv-2502-08300.creator: Eran Igra 1,2
arxiv-2502-08300.description: Abstract . Given a three-dimensional vector field F F with a finite number of fixed points - what can we say on its unbounded dynamics? We tackle this question, and prove sufficient conditions for F F to have fixed points with unbounded invariant manifolds.

arxiv-2504-08966.title: PACT: Pruning and Clustering-Based Token Reduction for Faster Visual Language Models
arxiv-2504-08966.creator: Mohamed Dhouib, Davide Buscaldi, Sonia Vanier, Aymen Shabou
arxiv-2504-08966.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohamed Dhouib, Davide Buscaldi, Sonia Vanier, Aymen Shabou. Visual Language Models require substantial computational resources for inference due to the additional input tokens needed to represent visual information. However, these visual tokens often contain redundant and unimportant information, resulting in an unnecessarily high number of tokens. To address this, we introduce PACT , a method that reduces inference time and memory usage by pruning irrelevant tokens and merging visually redundant ones at an early layer of the language model.

pmc-10649786.title: The Addition of Co into CuO–ZnO Oxides Triggers High Antibacterial Activity and Low Cytotoxicity
pmc-10649786.creator: Elvira Maria Bauer, Alessandro Talone, Patrizia Imperatori, Rossella Briancesco, Lucia Bonadonna, Marilena Carbone, Alexander Gusev
pmc-10649786.description: In the present work, a simple two-step method is proposed for mixed oxide synthesis aimed at the achievement of antibacterial nanomaterials. In particular, Cu, Zn and Co have been selected to achieve single-, double- and triple-cation oxides. The synthesized samples are characterized by XRD, IR, SEM and EDX, indicating the formation of either crystalline or amorphous hydrocarbonate precursors.

pmc-11341551.title: The use of hyaluronic acid in a 3D biomimetic scaffold supports spheroid formation and the culture of cancer stem cells
pmc-11341551.creator: Gamze Demirel, Yaprak Donmez Cakıl, Gursel Koltuk, Ranan Gulhan Aktas, Mahmut Calıskan
pmc-11341551.description: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting culture models capable of reproducing the pathological architecture of diseases are increasingly advancing. In this study, 3D scaffolds were created using extrusion-based bioprinting method with alginate, gelatin, and hyaluronic acid to investigate the effects of hyaluronic acid on the physical properties of the bioscaffold as well as on the formation of liver cancer spheroids.

pmc-11693788.title: Exploring the Intricacies of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia and Its Connection with HPV: A Narrative Review
pmc-11693788.creator: Parvin Karimi, Seyed Mohammad Reza Hosseini, Zahra Sadat Mousavian Hiagh, Sobhan Aboulhassanzadeh, Nahid Asghari, Hamed Aghazadeh
pmc-11693788.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia grade III (CIN III) represents a critical precursor to invasive cervical cancer, necessitating a comprehensive understanding of its etiology, progression, diagnosis, and preventive strategies. This review integrates an approach to synthesize current literature, conducted through a meticulous search of databases (Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar) for relevant articles discussing CIN III and its association with Human Papillomavirus (HPV).

pmc-12568568.title: Mitochondrial genome of Isatis indigotica reveals repeat-mediated recombination and phylogenetic insights in Cruciferae
pmc-12568568.creator: Shaoshuai Yu, Meiling Qin, Emmanuel Fleming, Xun Gong, Min Tang
pmc-12568568.description: Isatis indigotica is an important medicinal plant extensively used in traditional Chinese medicine for its antiviral and anti-inflammatory properties. While previous studies have elucidated its nuclear and plastid genomes, the mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) —critical for understanding organellar evolution, intracellular DNA transfer, and stress response mechanisms—has remained uncharacterized.

pmc-13180167.title: Prontuário Compassivo: Development and initial assessment of a palliative care digital platform in socially vulnerable contexts
pmc-13180167.creator: Janaína Santos Nascimento, Liana Amorim Corrêa Trotte, Livia Costa de Oliveira, Maria Gefé da Rosa Mesquita, Virgílio Garcia Moreira, Alexandre Ernesto Silva, Bruna Cezar Diniz, Glaziela Arruda Coelho, Ana Paula Correa Ferreira, Thiago Crispino, Márcia de Sousa Murta, Fernanda Carvalho de Queiroz Me
pmc-13180167.description: Introduction:Structured clinical records are essential for ensuring the quality and continuity of palliative care, particularly in socially vulnerable contexts. Existing digital systems rarely capture psychosocial or subjective data, limiting interdisciplinary collaboration and person-centered care planning.Objective:To describe the development and preliminary usability assessment of Prontuário Compassivo, a Brazilian digital platform designed to support clinical documentation and coordination of community-based palliative care.

pmc-13238727.title: Reduced incidence of arrest following an extreme risk protection order among respondents in California
pmc-13238727.creator: Veronica A Pear, Julia P Schleimer, Aaron B Shev, Garen J Wintemute, Shannon Frattaroli, April M Zeoli, Charles Branas
pmc-13238727.description: Extreme risk protection orders (ERPOs) are used to disarm individuals making threats of interpersonal harm, but little is known about respondents’ pre- and postorder criminal behavior. We sought to quantify ERPO respondents’ rate of arrest vis-à-vis timing of the order.

pmc-13477412.creator: Yumi Obata, Sachi Shimmi, Yusuke Seino, Atsuko Kamijo-Ikemori, Soichiro Inoue
pmc-13477412.description: BackgroundAcute kidney injury (AKI) following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a major predictor of poor postoperative outcomes. Post-TAVI AKI is considered a multifactorial syndrome involving renal functional reserve, tubular injury, and systemic inflammation; however, reliable preoperative stratification methods remain limited.

uslaw-usc-t22-s1645g.title: 22 U.S.C. § 1645g — Consolidated awards
uslaw-usc-t22-s1645g.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s1645g.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 21 (Settlement Of International Claims); Subchapter VII (Claims Against Vietnam). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. With respect to any claim under section 1645b of this title which, at the time of the award, is vested in persons other than the person by whom the original loss was sustained, the Commission shall issue.
